final_recommendations.description:
Optional next-step suggestions for the
parent (e.g., "prioritize testing X", "spawn an agent to
cover Y").
final_recommendations.title: Final Recommendations

findings.description:
Optional bullet list of confirmed observations. For
credit-bearing vulnerabilities, file
``create_vulnerability_report`` first (or
``create_dependency_report`` for dependency CVEs); this is
for narrative.
findings.title: Findings

report_to_parent.description:
Whether to deliver the completion report to
the parent's inbox. Default ``True``.
report_to_parent.title: Report To Parent

result_summary.description:
What you accomplished and discovered. Concrete
and specific (URLs, parameters, payloads that worked).
result_summary.title: Result Summary

success.description:
Whether the assigned subtask was completed
successfully. Default ``True``.
success.title: Success

patch.description: Complete `apply_patch` payload. Follow the tool description exactly.

inherit_context.description:
Default ``True``. The child receives the
parent's input history as background; only set ``False``
when starting a clean-slate task.
inherit_context.title: Inherit Context

name.description:
Human-readable child name (used in graph views and
``send_message_to_agent`` flows).
name.title: Name

skills.description:
List of skill names (e.g. ``["xss", "sql_injection"]``).
Max 5; prefer 1-3.
skills.title: Skills

task.description:
Specific objective. Be concrete — what to test, what
success looks like, any constraints.
task.title: Task

advisory_cvss.description:
**Required.** Published advisory base score
(0.0-10.0) — read it off the advisory (trivy CVSS / NVD / GHSA).
Severity is derived solely from this score, so it must be the
real published value; do not guess or omit it.
advisory_cvss.title: Advisory Cvss

dependency_path.description:
The resolution chain from the direct dependency
to the vulnerable package, joined with `` > `` (e.g.
``express@4.18.1 > body-parser@1.20.0 > qs@6.10.2``). Omit
for direct dependencies.
dependency_path.title: Dependency Path

description.description: What the CVE is and why the pinned version is affected.
description.title: Description

impact.description: What the CVE enables; business risk in this context.
impact.title: Impact

introduced_by.description:
For a **transitive** dependency, the direct
dependency (from the project's own manifest) that pulls the
vulnerable package in, as ``name@version`` (e.g.
``express@4.18.1``). Omit when the vulnerable package is
itself a direct dependency.
introduced_by.title: Introduced By

manifest_path.description:
**Required.** The repo-relative path of the
lockfile/manifest where the vulnerable version was observed —
trivy's ``Target`` (e.g. ``package-lock.json``,
``services/api/pom.xml``). Strip any scan-workspace or repo
checkout directory prefix so the path is relative to the
repository root. This binds the finding to its exact file so
remediation can target the right repository.
manifest_path.title: Manifest Path

reachability.description:
Usage-evidence level from static analysis — one of
``not_imported`` / ``imported`` / ``vulnerable_symbol_used`` /
``reachable_call_path`` / ``unknown``. Claim only what the
evidence proves; when in doubt use ``unknown``.
reachability.title: Reachability

reachability_evidence.description:
The concrete proof for the claimed level
(required for any level other than ``unknown``): repo-relative
``file:line`` of the import or symbol usage, the matched
advisory symbols, or the govulncheck call-path excerpt.
reachability_evidence.title: Reachability Evidence

remediation_steps.description: How to fix (usually upgrade to a fixed version).
remediation_steps.title: Remediation Steps

category.description: One of the categories above. Default ``"general"``.
category.title: Category

content.description: Full note body. Markdown is preserved.
content.title: Content

todos.description:
JSON array of todo objects. For one todo, pass a one-item
list. Each object's fields:

- ``title`` (str, **required**): short actionable title,
  e.g. ``"Test /api/admin for IDOR"``.
- ``description`` (str, optional): extra context or
  acceptance criteria.
- ``priority`` (str, optional): one of ``"low"`` /
  ``"normal"`` / ``"high"`` / ``"critical"``. Anything else,
  including omitting it, falls back to ``"normal"`` rather
  than failing.

Example: ``[{"title": "Probe /admin", "priority": "high"},
{"title": "Check JWT alg=none"}]``.
todos.title: Todos

todo_ids.description:
JSON array of todo IDs to delete. For one todo, pass
a one-item list.
todo_ids.title: Todo Ids

login.description: Whether to run the shell with -l/-i semantics. Defaults to true.
login.title: Login

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to return. Excess output will be truncated.
max_output_tokens.title: Max Output Tokens

shell.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell.
shell.title: Shell

tty.description: Whether to allocate a TTY for the command. Defaults to false (plain pipes); set to true to open a PTY and access TTY process.
tty.title: Tty

workdir.description: Optional working directory to run the command in; defaults to the turn cwd.
workdir.title: Workdir

yield_time_ms.description: How long to wait (in milliseconds) for output before yielding.
yield_time_ms.title: Yield Time Ms

note_id.description: Note id from ``create_note`` or a ``list_notes`` entry.
note_id.title: Note Id

report_id.description:
Report id from ``list_reports`` or a
``create_vulnerability_report`` / ``create_dependency_report``
response (format ``vuln-NNNN``).
report_id.title: Report Id

include_content.description:
When False (default) entries have a preview;
when True the full ``content`` is included.
include_content.title: Include Content

search.description: Substring match against title and content.
search.title: Search

tags.description: Filter to notes that have any of these tags.
tags.title: Tags

include_details.description:
When False (default) entries are compact; when
True full report bodies are returned.
include_details.title: Include Details

search.description: Substring match against title and description.
search.title: Search

target.description: Substring match against a report's target / endpoint.
target.title: Target

scope_id.description: Restrict to a Caido scope (managed via ``scope_rules``).
scope_id.title: Scope Id

depth.description:
``"DIRECT"`` (immediate children) or ``"ALL"``
(recursive subtree). Only meaningful with ``parent_id``.
depth.title: Depth

parent_id.description: Entry ID to expand; omit for root domains.
parent_id.title: Parent Id

scope_id.description:
Limit roots to a Caido scope (only used when
``parent_id`` is omitted). Manage scopes via ``scope_rules``.
scope_id.title: Scope Id

skills.description:
List of skill names (e.g. ``["xss", "sql_injection"]``).
Max 5. Names match the bare files under
``strix/skills/<category>/<name>.md``.
skills.title: Skills

todo_ids.description:
JSON array of todo IDs to mark done. For one todo,
pass a one-item list.
todo_ids.title: Todo Ids

todo_ids.description:
JSON array of todo IDs to reset to pending. For one
todo, pass a one-item list.
todo_ids.title: Todo Ids

modifications.description:
Patch dict. Recognized keys:

- ``url`` — replace the URL.
- ``params`` — dict of query-string keys to add/update.
- ``headers`` — dict of headers to add/update.
- ``body`` — replace the body string entirely.
- ``cookies`` — dict of cookies to add/update.
modifications.title: Modifications

action.description:
- ``list`` — return all scopes.
- ``get`` — single scope by ``scope_id``.
- ``create`` — needs ``scope_name``, optionally
  ``allowlist`` / ``denylist``.
- ``update`` — needs ``scope_id`` + ``scope_name``;
  allowlist / denylist replace the previous values.
- ``delete`` — needs ``scope_id``.
action.title: Action

message.description:
The full message body. Be specific — include payloads,
URLs, or what you want them to do, not just headlines.
message.title: Message

message_type.description:
``query`` (you want a reply), ``instruction``
(you're directing them), ``information`` (FYI, no reply
expected). Default ``information``.
message_type.title: Message Type

cascade.description:
If ``True`` (default), also stop every descendant of
``target_agent_id`` leaves-first. ``False`` stops only the
target.
cascade.title: Cascade

reason.description:
Optional human-readable reason for the stop, surfaced
in logs and telemetry.
reason.title: Reason

target_agent_id.description:
The 8-char id from ``view_agent_graph`` /
``create_agent``. Cannot stop yourself.
target_agent_id.title: Target Agent Id

thought.description: The reasoning to record. Must be non-empty.
thought.title: Thought

tags.description: New tags list, or ``None`` to keep.
tags.title: Tags

updates.description:
JSON array of update objects. For one update, pass a
one-item list. Each object's fields:

- ``todo_id`` (str, **required**): ID returned by
  ``create_todo``.
- ``title`` (str, optional): new title.
- ``description`` (str, optional): new description (empty
  string clears it).
- ``priority`` (str, optional): one of ``"low"`` /
  ``"normal"`` / ``"high"`` / ``"critical"``.
- ``status`` (str, optional): one of ``"pending"`` /
  ``"in_progress"`` / ``"done"``.

Omitted fields stay unchanged. Example:
``[{"todo_id": "abc", "status": "in_progress",
"priority": "high"}]``.
updates.title: Updates

path.description: Path to the image file. Absolute and relative workspace paths are supported.
path.title: Path

search_pattern.description:
Optional regex; switches the response shape to
compact hits.
search_pattern.title: Search Pattern

reason.default: Waiting for messages from other agents
reason.description:
One-line note shown in graph snapshots while you're
waiting (helps a human or sibling agent debug who's stuck
on what).
reason.title: Reason

timeout_seconds.description:
Max seconds to wait (default 300, and values above
that are cut short by a hard ceiling). This is only
a cap — the tool returns the INSTANT a message arrives, so a
larger value never makes you wait longer when the reply does
come. Right-size it to what you're waiting on: a short wait
(e.g. 10-60s) for a quick ack or a small/fast subtask, and a
longer one (e.g. ~100-200s) only for genuinely long-running
work (deep recon, exploitation, a full sub-scan). The cap only
bites when the expected message never arrives — so an oversized
timeout on a trivial wait just strands you idle until it
elapses. On timeout the tool returns and you decide whether to
keep working or wait again.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

query.description:
The search query — a full sentence with version numbers,
target tech, and the specific question. Treat it like a
ticket title for a senior security engineer.
query.title: Query
